News.title: Moment Uber driver is arrested and tries to destroy phone after luring woman into his car and raping her at knifepoint
News.content:
THIS is the moment an Uber driver tries to destroy his phone after being arrested for raping a woman in his car at knifepoint.

Adam Daley, 33, has been jailed for 16 years after luring the victim and her friend into his car after spotting them outside a bar in Leicester city centre.



Leicestershire Police have released footage showing Daley picking the women up and bodycam video of his arrest on December 29, 2025.

The video shows Daley getting out of his white Toyota Auris and approaching the women while he offers them a ride home.



The pair were about to order an Uber when Daley said he’d drive them if they booked the trip through the app, to which they agreed.

But after dropping her friend home, Daley started making sexualised comments towards the victim as they continued the journey to her address.



As they drove out of the city, Daley pulled over in a layby, claiming he needed to go to the toilet.

He then ordered the victim to move into the front of the car before touching her inappropriately and forcing her to perform oral sex on him by threatening her with a knife.



After the victim pleaded with Daley to stop, he sped off, leaving her in the layby where she called the police at 5.30am.

Officers quickly identified Daley’s registration and car model, and he was stopped at the junction of Vaughan Way and Great Central Street at 6.37am.

Footage shows Daley being put into handcuffs by a group of officers – but when he’s being helped out of the car, he tries to grab his phone and stamp on it to destroy any incriminating evidence.



He’s then placed in the back of a police vehicle where he’s read his rights.

Despite the victim’s DNA being found on Daley’s clothes and body, he continued to deny the horrific incident.

Mobile phone data also showed that Daley had driven past the victim in the layby three times after he left her there.

On July 10 at Leicester Crown Court, Daley was found guilty of one count of rape, one count of sexual assault, one count of possession of a bladed article and one count of threats to kill.

Daley was sentenced to a total of 16 years’ imprisonment and is subject to a Sexual Harm Prevention Order until further notice and a restraining order preventing him from contacting the victim.



Daley also pleaded guilty to two counts of drug driving after a drugs wipe and blood test revealed he was under the influence of cocaine during the incident.

At Leicester Magistrates’ Court on April 1, he was banned from driving for 20 months, fined £200 and ordered to pay £85 court costs and an £80 victim surcharge.

Detective Constable Matt Smith from Signal – the force’s dedicated rape and serious sexual assault team is the officer in the case.

He said: “I want to commend the victim in this case during what has been an extremely difficult six months.

“Her actions that night and the strength and bravery she has shown during the investigation and trial has ensured a dangerous individual is now behind bars.



“Despite her deeply traumatic and distressing experience, that night she demonstrated exceptional presence of mind and was able to contact police immediately after Daley had driven off.

“Thanks to this, officers were able to act quickly to identify and locate the suspect in a very short space of time.

“This was crucial to our investigation and ensured not only key forensic evidence could still be detected but that he was apprehended before he attacked anyone else.

“Daley targeted a lone woman after she trusted him to get her home safely. Given his job as an Uber driver it is possible there could be more victims that have not come forward.

“We take reports of sexual assault very seriously and anyone who wishes to report offences will be spoken to by specialist officers in the team.”

News.title: Andy Burnham set to soften migrant rules despite backing Shabana Mahmood’s new asylum crackdown
News.content:
ANDY Burnham last night backed the Home Secretary’s new asylum crackdown – but tougher migrant settlement rules look set to be softened under his premiership.

The Prime Minister-in-waiting voted for Shabana Mahmood’s new law, which will make it easier to deport illegal migrants and foreign criminals.



It will also curb the use of human rights laws to block removals, speeds up asylum appeals and forces migrants to repay the cost of taxpayer-funded accommodation.

But the incoming Government is already facing claims it is preparing to “capitulate to open border MPs” by softening separate settlement reforms.



Ministers are preparing concessions to plans to double the wait for indefinite leave to remain from five years to ten.

One proposal would allow up to 1.6 million “Boriswave” migrants already living in Britain to keep the five-year route to settlement.

Instead, they would have to wait longer before claiming benefits.

The compromise is aimed at heading off a Labour backlash after almost 80 MPs urged Mr Burnham to rethink the tougher settlement rules.

Mr Burnham has previously questioned applying the changes to migrants already living in Britain.

Yesterday, however, his spokesperson made clear he fully backed Ms Mahmood’s asylum crackdown.



He said: “Andy believes the public deserve an asylum system that is both compassionate and credible.

“This Bill takes important steps towards restoring confidence by tackling illegal crossings while strengthening safe and legal routes for genuine refugees. This is about ensuring the system is fair both to those seeking protection and to the communities that welcome them.”

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp challenged Ms Mahmood over whether she and the incoming Prime Minister were preparing to “capitulate to some of their open border MPs” on the settlement reforms.

The Home Secretary insisted the Government’s position remained “exactly as was set out in the consultation”.

News.title: Huge parts of Britain now at risk of wildfires – see if your area is affected
News.content:
WILDFIRES were raging across Britain yesterday in vast areas turned tinder-dry by the latest heatwave.

Families were evacuated as huge flames came within yards of their homes.



Major incidents were declared as hundreds of firefighters battled blazes on moorland.

The clouds of smoke and ash were also swept across towns and cities.



In North Wales, villagers near Conwy Mountain and the Sychnant Pass road had to flee their homes and the public were warned to avoid the area as a major fire raged for a second day.

Residents of the hillside hamlet of Capelulo were advised to “leave safely and follow the instructions of the emergency services on scene”.

Local Ben Campbell said: “The sound was worse than anything. It was so loud, the crackling. You could hear it coming down the mountain.”

North Wales was also hit by two 39739184 in Gwynedd and another in Flintshire.



Another fierce blaze in Oldham, Gtr Manchester, was thought to have been started by fireworks let off in memory of Karl Holland, 18, who drowned in Dovestones reservoir on Friday.

A woman aged 20 was yesterday arrested on suspicion of arson, police confirmed.

In the Peak District, fire crews were back tackling a blaze that first started on June 24 on Tintwistle Moor near Glossop, Derbyshire.



Fires also erupted in London, Co Durham, Hampshire, East and West Sussex, Devon and Somerset, echoing the string of blazes seen across parched southern Europe.

And the summer’s third heatwave also claimed the life of a dad who died saving his children from the sea.

He and a passing dog walker ran in to save his son and daughter when they were swept out at Seaton Carew, Co Durham, on Sunday.

The children were rescued but both men were declared dead after being pulled from the water by the RNLI.

More than 30 people have drowned while swimming in open water during this year’s hot spells.

News.title: Family birds of prey event cancelled after threats from woke vegans
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FOWL PLAY Family birds of prey event cancelled after threats from woke vegans

A BIRDS of prey flying display has been ­cancelled after pressure from vegans.

Organisers say they axed the free family event despite having all welfare standards in place.



Animal rights groups are thrilled the display, which would have featured eagles, falcons and hawks, has been canned.

It was to take place this month at Hopetown Darlington museum, County Durham.



A spokesman at the attraction said: “While all appropriate welfare, accreditation and safety standards were in place, we have listened to the concerns raised by local campaign groups and have taken the decision to cancel the birds of prey flying display.”

Darlington Vegans, Freedom for Animals, and North East Animal Rights campaigners sent a series of emails urging the venue not to use living creatures at events.

Darlington Vegans’ Kathy Barley said these displays “force wild animals to perform unnatural behaviour”.

Kathy added: “[We] are delighted to hear the event has been cancelled.

“Rather than promoting a genuine understanding of raptor ecology it reinforces the harmful idea that wildlife exists for human exploitation.”

Freedom for Animals said it is calling for “a more compassionate approach to engaging the public with wildlife”.



It added the cancellation proves “speaking up for animals can make a difference”.

News.title: Dad is charged after Brit boy, 3, ‘fell from arms & out 4th-floor window while playing aeroplane’
News.content:
HOLIDAY HORROR Dad is charged after Brit boy, 3, ‘fell from arms & out 4th-floor window while playing aeroplane’

A BRIT dad has been charged with negligence over the death of his three-year-old son who fell out of a fourth floor hotel window in Cyprus.

The boy reportedly slipped from his dad’s arms while they were playing “aeroplane”, and plunged 33ft to the veranda below.



The 37-year-old dad was arrested after the horrific family-holiday tragedy in Chloraka, Paphos on Sunday.

An ambulance was called to the scene, but when paramedics arrived they found the child was not responding.



He was taken to Paphos General Hospital where doctors pronounced him dead.

The family had only arrived at the hotel for their two-week holiday stay around 40 minutes before chaos struck.



The pair, along with the boy’s grandfather, had left their rooms and were heading towards the elevator to go to dinner.

While they were waiting for it to arrive, the dad was holding the child aloft.

There was a double window next to where they were standing, measuring roughly 4ft wide and 8ft tall.

The toddler somehow fell through the opening, suffering “severe cranial wounds and multiple wounds to his body and vital organs” in the ordeal.



Local cops received initial reports of the terrifying plunge at around 6.40pm that night.

The tragic boy’s family have another five-year-old girl, who is also with them on the holiday.

In the aftermath of the tragic incident, the distraught parent was taken into custody.



The dad, who has not been identified, appeared at Paphos District Court yesterday morning charged with causing death through negligence.

His family are in the process of finding a legal representative, he said as he appeared in court without a lawyer.

According to local media, he broke down in tears in the dock before proceedings had to be paused.

Authorities have taken five statements so far as part of an investigation into the incident.

The dad was remanded in custody for eight days – the maximum length the police can apply for.



If convicted, the parent could face up to four years in prison.

Police spokesman Vyron Vyronos said “the father may be released before the remand expires”, if the police probe is completed earlier.

Cops are scouring CCTV footage from the luxury hotel as inquiries continue.

IN THE DOCK MP ‘groped women’s breasts at celeb club after pestering them for drinks’

AN MP groped the breasts of two women at a celeb hangout after pestering them to drink with him, a court has heard.

Patrick Spencer is accused of drunkenly touching the women at the private members’ club in August 2023.



Jurors heard the women told each other what happened and Spencer left The Groucho Club in ­Soho, central London, after a ­confrontation at the bar.

Neither woman knew Spencer, 38, who was at the club as a guest.



He was later identified from his profile image on the House of Commons website.

Spencer told cops he hugged a friend from behind and did the same to the women, believing they were in the same group.

Prosecutor Polly Dyer said: “He described his behaviour as not appropriate in this day and age.”

The married dad of two was elected MP for ­Central Suffolk and North Ipswich in 2024 while the alleged assaults were under investigation.

The Conservative Party removed the whip in 2025, and he now sits as an independent MP.

Spencer, of Woodbridge, Suffolk, denies sex assaults.



The trial at Southwark crown court continues.

News.title: Andy Burnham’s migration plans must be properly scrutinised as they are SOFTER than even Starmer’s Government wanted
News.content:
Border games

ANDY Burnham doesn’t officially become Prime Minister until next week but he is already playing games over immigration.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood won plaudits earlier this year for her tough plans to get a grip on our borders.



Burnham is now letting it be known that he will support her.

Except all is not as it seems.



The plans the Home Secretary is bringing forward have been quietly watered down to appease Left-wing Labour MPs.

Up to 1.6million migrants who came to Britain in the uncontrolled wave of arrivals in 2021 could now be granted indefinite leave to remain after just FIVE years — instead of the TEN initially proposed by Mahmood.

Far from being tough on migration, Burnham supports a plan that is SOFTER than even Keir Starmer’s Government wanted.

Burnham’s feet should be held to the fire over this.

Instead, MPs will head off on holiday on Thursday until September.

That means NONE of Mr Burnham’s first actions after becoming PM the following Monday will be properly scrutinised for weeks.



What a blatant affront to democracy.

Calamity cops

WHY are the cops so incapable of trusting the public with information?

The appalling communications failures by police in the wake of the Southport murders in 2024 were supposed to be a watershed moment.

Yet, instead of opting for transparency, senior officers have again created confusion in their handling of Ann Widdecombe’s murder.

Not all the facts in the case have been established.



But we DO know the police made a mess of the public pronouncements they did make.

Hints were wrongly dropped of a burglary gone wrong, and the public was informed there was NO evidence that Ann’s violent death was “political” or that it was terrorism.

Repeatedly, the public was given finger-wagging instructions not to speculate.

Now it transpires the suspect — a loner with no known connection to Ann who lived 300 miles away — has been re-arrested on suspicion of terrorism.

We will find out if police had good reasons for this sudden U-turn.



But the worry is they’ve already further damaged public trust and confidence.

British forever

TIRESOME Argentinians may see their World Cup semi-final with England as an excuse for more boorish sabre-rattling over the Falklands.

But Messi and his pals can sing their moronic chants all they like.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As long as the union flag flies over Port Stanley, the islands remain OURS.

PM-in-waiting Andy Burnham should send out a clear message to the islanders that he has got their backs.

News.title: Moment US blows up Iran naval base using kamikaze drone boats as third night of strikes unfolds
News.content:
THIS is the moment US forces blow up an Iranian port with kamikaze drone boats – the first time the weapons have ever been used in combat.

Dramatic footage shows the vessels glide across the water before blitzing Bandar Abbas Naval Base – the regime’s navy headquarters.



The attacks are the latest in a series of tit-for-tat strikes across the Strait of Hormuz as the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed on June 17 lies in tatters.

Clips released by US Central Command show three different attacks – each blowing up a port in a shower of smoke and sparks.



The kamikaze boats struck a submarine and a ship maintenance facility in a mission hailed as “successful” by US Central Command.

The Saronic Corsair, a 24ft autonomous boat, can reach a speed of 35 knots (40mph) carrying up to 1,000lb of payload.



It can launch long-range strikes reaching targets as far as 1,000 nautical miles away.

In a post on X, the US said the strikes would “degrade” Iran’s ability to attack commercial vessels passing through the waterway.



It comes as the US launched its third consecutive night of attacks against Iran on Monday.

US President Donald Trump warned Iran would be “hit hard” today and tomorrow, with the country’s “Pickaxe Mountain” complex among targets.

Tehran retaliated, with the Islamic ​Revolutionary ‌Guard Corps claiming it pummelled US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait.

Earlier, Trump announced plans to shut down the Strait of Hormuz for Iranian vessels – and set a toll of 20 per cent on all ships attempting to pass.

Trump said on Truth Social on Monday: “We are reinstating the THE IRANIAN BLOCKADE, so named because it is only stopping Iran’s ships or customers from entering or leaving.



“All other countries will have fair and open use of the Strait.”

He noted that this also meant, “as a matter of FAIRNESS”, that Washington would be “reimbursed, at the rate of 20% on all cargo shipped”.

Trump said the process would “begin immediately”. It is unclear how exactly the US will charge the 20 per cent fee on all passing cargo vessels, or how it will protect them.



Iran had already announced over the weekend that the strait would be closed “until further notice”.

The regime’s foreign minister mocked the decision and said it would control the waterway “forever”.

Trump’s declaration comes amid a series of fresh strikes between Iran and the US which kicked off last week.

Both sides have accused each other of breaking the ceasefire and Tehran has declared ownership of the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian state media reports that the US has hit the Khuzestan province overnight.



Missile alarm sirens have also been heard in Bahrain, the country’s interior ministry said.

It comes as the UAE’s ministry of defence reports one crew member killed and several injured after two tankers were hit in the Strait by Iranian missiles.

United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre also reported that a vessel was hit by an “unknown projectile” near the Omani coast.

Last week, Trump declared the temporary peace deal – the memorandum of understanding – was “over” as Washington and Tehran launched a series of attacks on each other.

The mullah regime has unleashed a volley of strikes on Gulf Arab states in response to US attacks – including Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan, and Oman.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump slammed “sick” Iran for “playing dirty” after Tehran hit 85 American military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait in overnight strikes on July 6.

The escalating cycle of violence has left negotiations between Tehran and Washington to end the war in tatters.
